Why_Track: Know where users come from and which pages they land on
Anti_Pattern: Don't create custom page_view — use PostHog autocapture

Why_Track: Measures which pre-built options attract users — content-market fit signal
Anti_Pattern: Don't track generic 'click' — track the SPECIFIC action with context
Giantiny_Note: Which template = which use case resonates

Why_Track: The moment user commits to trying the product — activation proxy
Anti_Pattern: Don't track page loads as 'starts' — track explicit action only

Why_Track: Did user get VALUE from the product? Completion = value delivered
Anti_Pattern: Don't track auto-complete — only user-initiated full runs
Giantiny_Note: Completion rate = your #1 metric at Stage 2

Why_Track: Measures intent for premium features before building them
Anti_Pattern: Don't add 10 CTAs — test 1 'Get Pro Recipes' button
Giantiny_Note: Fake door test: measure clicks before building

Why_Track: Conversion from visitor to identified user
Anti_Pattern: Don't require signup before value — let users try first
Giantiny_Note: Signup AFTER value (not before). Pieter Levels pattern

Why_Track: Did they finish setup? Drop-off here = UX problem
Giantiny_Note: If >30% drop off at onboarding → simplify

Why_Track: Which features get used repeatedly? 80/20 rule: 1 feature = 80% usage
Anti_Pattern: Don't track every micro-interaction — track feature-level actions
Giantiny_Note: Feature concentration = know your real value prop

Anti_Pattern: Don't celebrate D1 return — D7 is the real test
Giantiny_Note: D7 retention > 20% = promising. < 10% = core loop broken (Reforge)

Why_Track: Organic growth signal — users become distributors
Anti_Pattern: Don't force invites — only track genuine sharing
Giantiny_Note: Viral coefficient: if <0.5 invites/user → product not remarkable enough

Anti_Pattern: Don't celebrate trial starts — track trial→paid conversion

Why_Track: Conversion that proves willingness to pay
Anti_Pattern: Don't auto-convert trials — measure genuine intent

Why_Track: Every churn is a learning opportunity — WHY did they leave?
Anti_Pattern: Don't just track churn count — capture the reason
Giantiny_Note: Revenue churn matters more than logo churn (ProfitWell)

Why_Track: Measure actual referral loop completion — not just link shares
Anti_Pattern: Don't count link shares as referrals — only completed signups
Giantiny_Note: Viral loop: Share→Visit→Signup→Activate must be <3 clicks

Why_Track: Support volume = proxy for UX problems or missing docs
Anti_Pattern: Don't ignore support patterns — they reveal product gaps
Giantiny_Note: If same issue >3x → fix the product not the docs (Giantiny ③)
